identified_issues: Phenomenological ambiguity: the observed pressure transient (-1.15 bar) and resonant acoustic peak (44.2 Hz) match both benign thermal duct contraction and catastrophic dynamic face seal fracture criteria.
Critical diagnostic sensor unavailability: secondary inter-seal sniffer HE-SNIFF-01 was offline for scheduled recalibration during the transient, preventing helium tracer verification.
Premature attribution of mechanical seal failure without distinguishing physical telemetry.
evidence: PT-401 registered a Delta-P of -1.15 bar, which falls precisely within the -1.0 to -1.3 bar range defined for both thermal contraction and seal fracture.
ACC-102 detected a resonant peak at 44.2 Hz, falling within the 40-48 Hz overlapping band common to both duct structural ringing and shaft resonance.
HE-SNIFF-01 log at 14:22:00.000Z indicates OFFLINE_CALIBRATION_PURGE with isolated port, resulting in N/A helium concentration telemetry and UNKNOWN integrity during the transient.
recommended_action: Hold test countdown progression under HELD status. Do not abort or commit to a definitive FAIL ruling until HE-SNIFF-01 is brought back online and an active helium buffer cavity leak check is conducted to differentiate seal rupture from duct thermal contraction.
